lesson_title: Acid Plus Base: The Colour Walk to Green
hook_text: Mix a dangerous acid with a dangerous base and you can get salty water. Here is the trick.
clip_script: Hydrochloric acid can burn skin. Sodium hydroxide can burn skin too. But mix them in exactly the right amounts and you get salty water. That is neutralisation: acid plus base gives salt plus water. The acid carries hydrogen ions, the base carries hydroxide ions, and when they meet they snap together into water. Watch it with universal indicator. The acid starts red. Add the base drop by drop and the colour walks: orange, yellow, green. Green means pH 7, perfectly cancelled. Overshoot and it turns blue, then purple, because now there is too much base. Boil off the water and white crystals of sodium chloride appear, the same salt as on your chips. You use neutralisation every day: antacids calm stomach acid, toothpaste fights acid on your teeth, and farmers spread lime on sour soil.
visual_style: A beaker on a white bench with drops falling in; colour sweeping from red to green and on to purple; ions pairing off into water molecules; salt crystals forming in a dish.
pacing: Tense opening about the hazards, then a slow, satisfying colour walk, a quick everyday finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to name every salt.
